html:
An early Iron Age farming culture of the forest steppe between the Dniester and Dnieper rivers in central Ukraine, from about 1025 to 700 BCE. The map shows it in 700 BCE.

Its people lived in villages of pit houses, grew wheat, barley and millet, and kept cattle and pigs. Along the edge of the steppe they built large earthwork forts, probably against the horsemen of the early Scythian and Cimmerian world to the south. They were among the first in the region to work iron.

The area matches where Herodotus later placed the Scythian ploughmen, farmers who grew grain under Scythian rule. Some scholars have seen the Chernoles people as ancestors of the early Slavs, but most now treat that link as unproven. To the west lay the Lusatian culture.
sum: An early Iron Age farming culture of the forest steppe between the Dniester and Dnieper rivers in central Ukraine, from about 1025 to 700 BCE. The map shows it in 700 BCE.
